topic: Tennis and golf: shoulder care for weekend players

slides.headline: Keep your shoulder in the weekend game
slides.sub: Four shoulder tips for tennis and golf players.

slides.title: Warm up before the first swing
slides.body: Five minutes of arm circles, band pull-aparts and easy swings or rallying helps your shoulder get ready. Many weekend players go straight to full power, which shoulders often dislike.

slides.title: Build load across the week
slides.body: A sudden jump, like a long tournament after weeks off, is a common trigger for sore shoulders. Where you can, play a little more often rather than a lot all at once.

slides.title: Strengthen the rotator cuff
slides.body: Side-lying external rotations and band rows, two or three times a week, help the shoulder handle repeated swings. Start light, three sets of 10 to 15, and build up gradually.

slides.title: Use your whole body
slides.body: Power in a serve or drive comes from the legs and trunk. If your hips and mid-back don't turn freely, the shoulder often ends up working harder. Mobility work for those areas helps.

slides.title: When to get it checked
slides.body: Pain that stops you sleeping on that side, weakness lifting the arm, a sudden pop with bruising, pins and needles down the arm, or pain that lasts more than a few weeks.

slides.headline: Keep playing with confidence
slides.body: Our Milton and Sunnybank physios assess your shoulder and the demands of your sport, then build a plan to keep you on the court or course. Book online — link in bio.

caption:
Great weekend of tennis or golf, sore shoulder by Monday? A few habits can help.

Warm up properly with arm circles and easy swings before going full power. Spread your playing across the week rather than one big jump. Strengthen your rotator cuff with side-lying rotations and band rows two or three times a week. And remember power comes from the legs and trunk, so stiff hips or mid-back can leave the shoulder doing extra work.

Get it checked if pain stops you sleeping on that side, you notice weakness lifting the arm, a pop with bruising, or pins and needles.

story.headline: Weekend swings, happy shoulders
story.body: Warm up first, spread your playing across the week, and strengthen your rotator cuff twice a week.
